\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian affine integral identity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_gaussian_affine_pair}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_gaussian_affine_pair}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianCombination}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $a\in\mathbb R^n$ and $b,c,v\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $c\ge
0$, $v\ge 0$, and $b^2+c^2=v^2$. For every strongly measurable function $f:\mathbb
R^n\to\mathbb R$, integrating $f(a+bZ+cW)$ over independent standard Gaussian vectors
$Z,W\in\mathbb R^n$ gives the same integral as integrating $f(a+vY)$ over a standard
Gaussian vector $Y\in\mathbb R^n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of a composed Gaussian noise integrand]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianNoise_compose_integrand}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianNoise_compose_integrand}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianEndpoint}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho,\sigma\in[-1,1]$, and let $f:\mathbb
R^n\to\mathbb R$ be integrable with respect to the product standard Gaussian measure
$\gamma_n$. For independent vectors $X,Y,Z$ with law $\gamma_n$, the function
$(x,y,z)\mapsto f\!\left(\sigma(\rho x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,y)+\sqrt{1-\sigma^2}\,z\right)$
is integrable with respect to the product law $\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Composition of Gaussian noise operators]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_compose_stronglyMeasurable}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_compose_stronglyMeasurable}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise_increment_variance, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianNoise_compose_integrand, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_gaussian_affine_pair}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho,\sigma\in[-1,1]$, and let $f:\mathbb
R^n\to\mathbb R$ be integrable and strongly measurable under the product standard
Gaussian measure. Applying the Gaussian noise operator at parameter $\sigma$ and then at
parameter $\rho$ agrees almost everywhere, under that measure, with applying it once at
parameter $\rho\sigma$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of a Gaussian noise pair product]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianNoise_pair_mul}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianNoise_pair_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianEndpoint}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$
each belong to $L^2(\gamma_n)$, where $\gamma_n$ is the product standard Gaussian
measure. If $X,Y$ are independent with law $\gamma_n$, then $(x,y)\mapsto f(x)g(\rho
x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,y)$ is integrable with respect to $\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Contraction of an integral in an $L^p$ norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.eLpNorm_integral_prod_le}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.eLpNorm_integral_prod_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $(alpha,mu)$ and $(beta,nu)$ be measurable spaces with measures, where $mu$ is
s-finite and $nu$ is a probability measure. If $1\le p\le\infty$ and
$F:\alpha\times\beta\to\mathbb R$ is strongly measurable almost everywhere with respect
to $mu\otimesnu$, then the function obtained by integrating $F(x,y)$ over $y$ has
$L^p(mu)$ norm at most the $L^p(mu\otimesnu)$ norm of $F$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Correlated Gaussian integral for integrable products]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_correlatedGaussianMeasure_of_integrable}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_correlatedGaussianMeasure_of_integrable}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianNoise}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\ge0$, let $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be such that
$(x,y)\mapsto f(x)g(y)$ is integrable under the joint distribution of $(X,Y)$ formed
from independent $X,W\sim\gamma_n$ by setting $Y=\rho X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,W$. Then
\[
\int f(x)g(y)\,d\mathcal L(X,Y)(x,y)=\int f(x)\left(\int g\bigl(\rho
x+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\,w\bigr)\,d\gamma_n(w)\right)d\gamma_n(x),
\]
where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure and $\mathcal L(X,Y)$ denotes that joint
measure.
\end{lemma}
